newsitem.title: HUNGARY: FORECAST-Hungary's govt. sec, yields seen dropping.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Hungary's govt. sec, yields seen dropping.

text.p: Hungarian government securities yields are seen dropping slightly this week, encouraged by recent central bank measures including rate cuts, dealers said.
"I expect a slight fall and the yields will go down at a slow pace later in the year," said Robert Schutt of Bank Austria Investment.
Traders said the National Bank of Hungary's (NBH) half percentage point repo rate cuts in the middle of June triggered a fall in government securities yields.
The NBH abolished its six-month and 12-month deposit facilities on Thursday and launched one-year bonds with a yield of 20.25 percent on Friday.
These measures led government securities yields further down by five to 20 basis points on the secondary market, dealers said.
They said the market was liquid, with funds placed into reverse repo deals before the repo rate cuts flowing back.
They added that the trend of decline in yields was likely to continue this week and the yields may drop further 10 to 20 basis points.
However, the 12-month discount Treasury bill will probably stay around 20.34 percent as the one-year NBH bond provided that bill with a strong support, dealers said.
They said that the yields on Treasury bills were likely to drop slightly at this week's auctions.
The Government Debt Managament Agency will auction one-month T-bills on Tuesday, three-month bills on Wednesday, six-month bills on Thuirsday and 12-month bills on Friday.
